title: Gut single-microbe landscape in patients with major depressive disorder and bipolar disorder
title_zh: 主要抑郁症与双相情感障碍患者肠道单菌景观
abstract: Microbial communities in the human gut are highly diverse and complex, and many play critical roles in health and disease. Their functioning depends not only on species composition and diversity but also on intra- and intercellular transcriptional dynamics. Robust technologies capable of capturing single-microbe RNA sequencing information are urgently needed to understand microbial heterogeneity and host interactions. In this exploratory study, we applied droplet-based single-microbe RNA sequencing (smRNA-seq2) to analyze gut microbiomes from five patients with major depressive disorder (MDD), five with bipolar disorder (BD), and five healthy participants (HP), generating a transcriptional atlas of 33,174 single microbial cells. Unsupervised clustering based on RNA expression profiles partitioned these cells into 37 distinct clusters, reflecting both taxonomic diversity and intra-species functional heterogeneity. The most dominant clusters were identified as Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans, Phocaeicola dorei, Enterocloster sp000431375, and Clostridium_Q sp003024715. Compositional and transcriptional differences were observed across diagnostic groups, with clustering patterns appearing to be influenced by disease, gender, and age. Functional heterogeneity was evident in oxidative stress and metabolic genes such as sodB, mdh2, and eno2 in Phocaeicola dorei, while stress-response genes (htpG_1, groL, dnaK, clpB) were upregulated in BD. Focusing on the ko03110 pathway (chaperones and folding catalysts), species-specific patterns emerged: Clostridium_Q_sp003024715 was positively associated with health but decreased in disease status; Enterocloster_sp000431375 and Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans were upregulated in BD; and Phocaeicola dorei was downregulated in MDD. Together, these findings suggest the presence of functional and phenotypic heterogeneity within the gut microbiome in mood disorders and identify exploratory microbial transcriptomic features that may be associated with group-level differences, warranting further validation in larger cohorts.
abstract_zh: 人类肠道微生物群高度多样且复杂，许多微生物在健康与疾病中发挥关键作用。其功能不仅取决于物种组成与多样性，还取决于细胞内外的转录动态。迫切需要能够捕获单菌RNA测序信息的稳健技术，以了解微生物异质性与宿主相互作用。本探索性研究中，我们采用基于微滴的单菌RNA测序（smRNA-seq2）分析了五名主要抑郁症（MDD）患者、五名双相情感障碍（BD）患者和五名健康对照（HP）的肠道微生物组，生成了33,174个单菌细胞的转录图谱。基于RNA表达谱的无监督聚类将这些细胞分为37个不同的簇，既反映了分类多样性，也体现了同种内功能异质性。最占优势的簇被识别为Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans、Phocaeicola dorei、Enterocloster sp000431375和Clostridium_Q sp003024715。不同诊断组之间在组成和转录上均存在差异，聚类模式似乎受到疾病、性别和年龄的影响。功能异质性在Phocaeicola dorei的氧化应激与代谢基因（如sodB、mdh2、eno2）中表现明显，而BD组的应激响应基因（htpG_1、groL、dnaK、clpB）上调。聚焦ko03110通路（分子伴侣与折叠催化剂）时，出现了物种特异性模式：Clostridium_Q_sp003024715与健康呈正相关但在疾病状态下降低；Enterocloster_sp000431375和Fusicatenibacter saccharivorans在BD中上调；Phocaeicola dorei在MDD中下调。综上所述，这些发现表明情绪障碍患者肠道微生物组存在功能与表型异质性，并识别出可能与群体水平差异相关的探索性微生物转录组特征，值得在更大人群中进一步验证。
